messages:
Lina: FYI customer 'acme-corp' opened a P1 — dedicated deployment behind their L7 LB started returning 403s for certain API routes after they flipped on SSO. error contains 'insufficient_scope'.
Kevin: do you have an example request/response?
Lina: yes — reproducer they gave (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...' https://dedicated.redwood.acme/api/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing required scopes: inference:create"}
```
Lina: if I hit the same backend pod IP (bypassing LB) with the same token it works fine: 200.
Devon: that screams header being stripped/mangled at the LB/proxy. what LB are they using?
Lina: GCP internal L7 + an OAuth2 proxy in front that they recently enabled for SSO. They said they configured it to 'forward' but looks like it's issuing signed cookies.
Kevin: could be opaque token exchange — auth proxy terminates Authorization and sets a cookie, backend sees no Authorization header and returns insufficient_scope. do we check for x-forwarded-authorization or a custom header?
Lina: backend only checks Authorization header. We don't have code to accept x-forwarded-authorization for dedicated/private deploys by default.
infra-bot: [automated] New network trace collected: trace-id=tr-1992356798.
Devon: can you drop the raw HTTP capture (curl -v) going to the LB and to the pod? headers matter.
Lina: pasted both captures below (token replaced with <TOK>):
--- to LB ---
> GET /api/v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: dedicated.redwood.acme
> Authorization: Bearer <TOK>
< HTTP/1.1 302 Found
< Set-Cookie: _oauth2_proxy=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure
< Location: /api/v1/generate
--- to pod (direct) ---
> GET /api/v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: internal-pod:8080
> Authorization: Bearer <TOK>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Lina: LB path goes through oauth2-proxy which does cookie dance and removes Authorization header.
Kevin: ok that explains it. customer-side change caused request-flow to stop passing bearer through. two options: 1) configure oauth2-proxy to forward original Authorization (if supported), 2) teach our gateway to accept forwarded header (e.g., X-Forwarded-Authorization) or signed-cookie -> introspect, 3) change routing to TCP passthrough if possible.
Devon: also need to check token type: if oauth2-proxy exchanged the incoming JWT for an opaque session cookie, the original token may not be present. Backend validation by scope fails.
Lina: customer said the SSO session is different from API auth — they expected LB to pass Authorization through. they added a note that it worked for embeddings endpoint but not for generation routes (different frontend routing rules).
Kevin: could be a path-specific auth filter in front causing header drop. Ask them for their envoy/ingress config.
Lina: they shared envoy filter snippet:
```
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        -- noop
      end
```
no obvious drop there. but they also have istio ext-authz enabled on /api/v1/generate.
Devon: istio ext-authz can return denials or mutate headers. check the ext-authz logs.
infra-bot: [automated] ext-authz request log: request_id=rid-9921 action=DENY reason="missing_authorization_header"
Kevin: ext-authz is denying because Authorization missing. So chain is: client -> oauth2-proxy (adds cookie, removes Authorization) -> envoy/istio -> backend. ext-authz sees no Authorization and denies.
Lina: suggested repro steps for customer (safe):
1) curl LB with explicit Authorization header and follow redirects: `curl -v -L -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOK>' https://dedicated.redwood.acme/api/v1/generate`
2) curl LB with `--cookie "_oauth2_proxy=..."` to simulate session cookie
3) curl pod IP directly with same Authorization header
Compare results.
Kevin: mitigation we can suggest: set oauth2-proxy to `pass_access_token = true` or enable `--pass-authorization-header` depending on proxy. For GCP's IAP there are different configs (IAP rewrites Authorization).
Devon: for cases where customers insist on SSO + API keys, recommend: use a separate ingress path for API callers that does not terminate oauth SSO, or use client-cert mutual TLS between LB and backend, or use header mapping like `x-original-authorization`.
Lina: I've asked customer to try toggling 'pass_authorization_header'. they responded: 'we tried that, didn't work; oauth2-proxy is running in front of the LB and doesn't support that flag in our version'
Kevin: fallback: we can add support in our dedicated gateway to accept `x-forwarded-authorization` if present and the source is a trusted LB IP. Security note: only accept forwarded auth from mutually authenticated clients or specific subnets.
Devon: file a ticket to engineering (ENG-PLATFORM) for a configurable header fallback. include controls: allowed trusted proxies, header name, strictness mode (deny if both present but mismatch).
Lina: opening ticket now: ENG-PLATFORM-987 - "support x-forwarded-authorization from trusted proxies for dedicated/private deployments". tagging @kevin @devon.
support-bot: [automated] Created support case INC-2025-451 for acme-corp, priority P1.
Kevin: short-term customer workaround: mint a dedicated API key bound to service account and pass it as `x-api-key` header — backend will accept it even if Authorization is consumed by SSO. But this requires policy change on their side.
Devon: long-term: we'll add a note in dedicated deployment docs about common LB/proxy auth pitfalls (oauth2-proxy, IAP, GCP LB cookieing, nginx oauth module). Lina please gather configs we've seen and I'll help draft the doc.
Lina: will do. also pushing a diagnostic helper we use in support: `curl -sI -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOK>' $url | egrep -i 'authorization|set-cookie|www-authenticate|location'`
Lina: any objections to us adding an advisory to the onboarding checklist: "if you terminate SSO at L7, ensure Authorization header is forwarded / enable pass-through for API traffic"
Kevin: +1. add recommended fixes and exact oauth2-proxy flags.
Devon: final action items:
- Lina: collect customer's envoy/istio/oauth2-proxy configs and add to ticket (due EOD)
- Kevin: prototype a minimal header-fallback change for the dedicated gateway (POC branch)
- Devon: draft KB entry for LB auth header pitfalls
Lina: ack. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [automated] Support trace closed for trace-id=tr-1992356798 at 1992360450.
